name: Allotrope Medical
long_description:
Allotrope Medical is a Houston-based medical device company founded and run by the surgeon that created the technology.

Our platform stimulation technology gives physicians control over the natural movements of the urinary and digestive systems. This control over smooth muscle tissues allows the surgeon to identify hidden anatomic structures (ureters, sphincters and others), determine tissue health, and even assist in diagnosing disease states. The technology is delivered through the surgeon's existing instruments (which have remained unchanged in over 30 years) giving a completely new capability to the surgeon while maintaining seamless workflow integration.

With an $600M (and growing)  initial market, the technology is future-proof and is readily able to be integrated into the continued advancements in the surgical space.
one_liner: Advancing surgical precision through safe electrical stimulation.

launches.title: Illuminant Surgical: A new way of seeing inside the human body
launches.tagline: Displaying images directly on the patient for safer, faster procedures
launches.body:
**💡TL;DR**

* We give doctors X-ray vision without the need for headsets or monitors.
* It works in any operating room, requires zero wearables, and seamlessly integrates into existing workflows.
* We're starting with spine surgery, pain management, and interventional radiology - 11M+ annual procedures in the U.S.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=65365&key=user_uploads/636938/0a341696-1b40-4543-b52f-2cc145a6579f)

**❌ The Problem: Patient Access Is Stuck In The 1800s**

Every year, hundreds of millions of procedures require precise access to internal anatomy. Whether placing a screw in the spine, inserting a needle for a biopsy, or advancing a catheter, precision is critical. Yet surgeons still rely on outdated tools: fluoroscopy, “feel”, and mental reconstruction, leading to inefficiencies, complications, and billions in unnecessary healthcare costs.

This has serious consequences:

* For patients – misplaced implants, vascular injuries, and nerve damage result in repeat procedures, extended hospital stays, and life-altering complications.
* For hospitals – preventable surgical revisions cost tens of billions annually in unnecessary expenses
* For surgeons – Cumbersome tools and methods that extend case time, increase cognitive load, and limit the number of patients they can treat.

Spine surgery and interventional access are two of the fastest-growing segments and also among the most accuracy-dependent.

In the US alone:

* 1.6 M spine surgeries where millimeters can mean the difference between mobility and disability.
* 9.5 M interventional procedures that rely on accurate percutaneous access to treat and diagnose hundreds of different conditions and diseases.

**This is a $10B+ unmet need.**

**🔎 Our Solution: See Inside The Patient in Real Time, Directly On The Body**

We’ve built a new way of seeing inside the human body: Skylight is the first real-time anatomical projection system built to solve the problems with patient access. Instead of forcing doctors to look away at a screen, Skylight projects anatomy directly onto the patient, like an AR display—but without headsets, wearables, or extra steps.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=65365&key=user_uploads/636938/8f98ebe8-aa8b-44e5-aac5-1b03d5105bfd)

To make this happen, we’ve developed a novel method of tracking the patient with sub-millimeter accuracy and we’ve built this system to be universally compatible with industry-standard tools and scanners to allow adoption without changing workflow.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=65365&key=user_uploads/636938/d4213fc6-0747-4211-8bc3-56a309fd14c9)

**Just as fiber optics revolutionized how we do laparoscopy and minimally invasive surgeries, anatomical projection will become the new standard for patient access.**

**Who We Are:**

We’re James and Eldrick, two Stanford engineers who first met as freshman dormmates and have now worked together for over a decade.

💉James: MD, bioengineer, scientist, and medical device builder.

⚙️ Eldrick: Experienced deep-tech founder. Built chips at Apple and led hardware-software teams at a lidar startup.

We’ve assembled a world-class team of engineers, clinicians, and medical device experts to solve tough problems at the intersection of medicine, computer vision, graphics, and hardware development.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=65365&key=user_uploads/636938/f5a0197a-718d-45cf-b2bd-f71769312830)

**We’re looking for:**

🩺 Clinicians → If you do spine, pain management, or IR, let’s talk.

🏥 Hospital Partners → Want to be at the forefront of procedural navigation? Reach out.

📰 Media → We’re redefining how doctors see. Let’s get the word out.

Email us [founders@illuminant.ai](mailto:founders@illuminant.ai) 💡

launches.title: Preload: Internet-scale touch data for physical AI
launches.tagline: What expert hands see, feel, and do, all in one dataset.
launches.body:
**TL;DR:** Preload captures how humans actually use their hands: what they see, what they feel, and what their muscles do. We turn that into training data that makes robots more dexterous. Robotics teams and partners: **email us at [surya@preload.ai](mailto:surya@preload.ai)**.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-HXgPwmEavA>

### **The problem**

Robots learn manipulation mostly from video. Video shows _what_ happened, but not _how_ it happened: how hard a hand gripped, where it made contact, or which muscles fired to make a movement smooth.

That missing signal is a big reason robots still struggle with dexterous tasks. Video alone can't teach a robot the force, contact, and intent behind human skill, and lab motion-capture rigs are too expensive and too slow to scale outside a controlled room.

### **What we built**

Preload is a wearable, multimodal data-capture stack that records human manipulation in the real world:

\- **Egocentric video:** what the person sees

\- **Tactile gloves:** contact and pressure across the whole hand

\- **EMG:** muscle activity that shows the _intent_ and effort behind each movement, not just the outcome

We time-sync all three streams into a single dataset, so models learn the full action: the scene, the contact, and the motor commands that produced it.

### **Why this matters**

Force and touch tell a robot what happened at the fingertips. EMG tells it _why_, because it captures the motor intent that comes before the motion. We believe that's the richest signal for teaching robots human-level dexterity, and it's hard to capture well without deep biosignal expertise.

### **Where we are**

\- Collecting data today in **real-world, non-surgical settings (350+ hours of data to date)**

\- **LOIs from major hospitals** to collaborate on capturing expert human skill

\- Long term, we're excited about **surgery**, where dexterity and precision matter most

### **The team**

We're PhD dropouts from **Johns Hopkins** and **Caltech** who have spent our careers capturing and decoding signals from the human body.

\- **Leo Li:** ex-Computational Neuroscience PhD candidate at Caltech. Previously a neuroengineer at **Neuralink** and a software engineer at **Amazon**. Robotics engineering (Eng Sci) degree from the University of Toronto.

\- **Surya Pandiaraju:** ex-BME PhD candidate at Johns Hopkins in neural dynamics and decoding. Previously at **Paradromics**, **NeuroPace**, **iota Biosciences**, and **Sonera Magnetics**. BME degree from the University of Waterloo.

\- **Runming (Tony) Wang:** ex-BME PhD candidate at Johns Hopkins School of Medicine. Builds neural recording and stimulation hardware, performs animal neurosurgeries, and previously studied motor-unit coordination with EMG and motion tracking at Emory and Georgia Tech.

### **Our ask**

\- **Robotics and physical AI teams:** if dexterous manipulation is your bottleneck, we'd love to talk about custom datasets. **Email [surya@preload.ai](mailto:surya@preload.ai)**

\- **Partners with skilled manual workflows:** if your team does precise, hands-on work, we'd love to collaborate on data collection

\- **We're hiring** across ML, robotics, sensors, software, hardware design, and field ops, plus Summer 2027 interns: **\[See open roles\]([https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/preload/jobs)](https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/preload/jobs%5C)**)\*\*
